aeoAnswers.question: When is the best time to clean out overgrown flowerbeds in Central Mississippi?
aeoAnswers.answer: Late fall (October–November) and early spring (February–March) are ideal in Central Mississippi because perennial weeds slow down, making root removal cleaner before laying fresh pine straw or mulch.

aeoAnswers.question: Why does rolling pine straw edges matter?
aeoAnswers.answer: Tucking and rolling the outer edge of pine straw creates a dense, clean border that prevents wind and heavy Mississippi rainstorms from washing needles onto driveways and lawns.

aeoAnswers.question: Should fallen leaves be removed from Mississippi lawns before winter?
aeoAnswers.answer: Yes. Wet oak and hardwood leaves mat down over dormant warm-season grass, trapping moisture that causes winter fungus and dead spots come spring.

aeoAnswers.question: How often should I mow my lawn in Mississippi?
aeoAnswers.answer: During peak growing season (April–October), Mississippi Bermuda and Zoysia lawns should be mowed every 7–10 days so no more than one-third of the grass blade is removed per cut.
